walkthroughs.body_html:
Exponentials & Logarithms — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exponentials & Logarithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exponentials & Logarithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an arithmetic and a geometric sequence?
options: Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.
Arithmetic sequences involve only addition and geometric sequences only multiplication, so 1, 2, 4 is arithmetic.
Arithmetic has a constant difference between terms; geometric has a constant ratio.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
-15, because two negatives multiply to give a larger negative result.
2 — subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so -3 + 5 = 2.
-8, because two negatives combine to make a bigger negative.
Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: -15, because two negatives multiply to give a larger negative result.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
